dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you?
Hi hon, yes, hi. Sorry, I'm on speaker, I'm in the car, so if I get choppy just tell me. I've got a drainage thing on my street that's driving me nuts.
Okay, no problem, I can hear you fine so far. What's going on, and where is it?

So it's 236 Coggeshall Avenue, up the Hill, Historic Hill. There's a puddle that goes across half the road, right in front of the house, and it will not drain. It hasn't rained in three days. Three days, hon. It's just sitting there.
Three dry days and still standing water. Is it near a storm drain, do you know?

Yeah, the drain's right at the low spot, at the edge of it. And I don't know if it's clogged or what, because it's just not going anywhere. And it's been like this, and honestly I feel like every time I call about something on this street it's a whole thing.
I hear you. Let me get this down properly. Is the water deep, or more of a wide shallow sheet?

Wide. Like, it takes up half the road, cars have to swing into the other lane to get around it. Ankle deep at the middle, I'd say. And there's something else, and maybe it's related. There's a manhole cover a little ways up from it, and it looks off. Like by an inch, maybe. It's not sitting flush.
Okay, that's good to know. Is it sitting higher than the pavement, or sunk lower, or just kind of crooked?
[pause] Crooked, I think. One side's higher. Cars go over it and it kind of clunks. I don't want somebody to blow a tire or worse.
Right, we'll put that in as a separate note so the crew looks at both. Is the water freezing at all overnight? It's been cold.

Yes! That's the other part. It's been getting icy at the edges in the morning, so now it's a skating rink and a puddle. And the school day starts at eight, so I'm out there at like seven-fifteen racing the clock, trying to get the kids across without anybody going down.
Oh, that's not great at all. Okay, I'm marking it as a hazard because of the ice. Let me make sure I have the address right, two thirty-six Coggeshall Avenue?
Two thirty-six, yep. Coggeshall, two g's, two l's, you know how it is.
I do. [pause] Okay, and the puddle is in front of your house, not down at a corner?
In front of the house, a little toward the downhill side. I'd say if you're looking at the house from the street, it's off to the left.
Got it. And has anybody from the city been out there for this before? I'm not seeing anything open on my screen yet.
No, nobody. I mean, I thought somebody else on the street would've called by now, but you know how that goes, everybody figures somebody else did it. So I'm just done waiting.
Fair enough. I'm going to send this to the crew that handles drains and road surface. I can't tell you exactly when they'll get out there, but with the ice I'll flag it to be looked at soon.
Okay. Soon like today, or soon like next week? Because I'm not trying to be pushy, hon, but it's been three days.
I can't promise a day. They're working through a list, but a hazard with ice goes toward the top of it. I'd rather tell you that straight.

No, I appreciate that. Honestly it's better than getting told tomorrow and then nothing. Can somebody call me back when it's done? Just so I know it's been taken care of and I'm not out there staring at it?
Absolutely. I'll put a request on the ticket for a callback when the work is finished. What's the best number?
It's 401-555-0167. That's my cell, I'll pick up, or leave a message if I'm in the school pickup line, I can't always grab it.
Okay, 401-555-0167. Name for the ticket?
Antonella Grasso. G-R-A-S-S-O.

Thank you, Antonella. So I've got a standing puddle across half the road in front of 236 Coggeshall, no rain for three days, icing in the mornings, and a manhole cover that's uneven by about an inch up the street. Callback when it's finished.
That's it exactly. And if the crew wants to talk to me, I'm usually around after nine, once the kids are dropped.
I'll add that to the notes. If anything changes in the meantime, I'd say keep the kids on the sidewalk side, away from that low spot.
Oh, we do, we do. We hug the wall like crazy people. Okay, thank you, hon. You have a good one.
You too, Antonella. Take care, and enjoy your lunch hour.
Ha, I wish. Bye now.
